content:
In the middle of all the rebellion of Numbers 16, one thing shines out clearly: what Moses did with a rebellious people. When they gathered against him,
he fell on his face (Numbers 16:4). When the plague broke out, he did not rejoice over the people's punishment but told Aaron to take the censer and run into the middle of the dying, saying, "Take it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them" (Numbers 16:46). And Aaron "stood between the dead and the living; so, the plague was stopped" (Numbers 16:48). This is the heart of it. The very people who had rejected Moses were the people Moses hurried to save. The man they blamed became the man who stood between them and death. Today we go straight to that one great act, intercession, and to the far greater One who does the same for us today.

Moses interceded for people who were rebelling against him. When Yahweh's wrath threatened the whole camp, Moses and Aaron fell on their faces and cried, "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and You be angry with all the congregation?" (Numbers 16:22). These were the very people who had listened to Korah and challenged his authority, yet when their lives were in danger, Moses did not step back and let them perish. He fell down and pleaded for them. This is exactly what we see in Christ, only far greater. Isaiah said of the Messiah, "He bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors" (Isaiah 53:12). And even while being crucified, Christ prayed, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do" (Luke 23:34).
Moses prayed for those who rebelled against him; Christ interceded for those who were nailing Him to the cross.

This is one of the clearest reasons Christ is called a Prophet like Moses.
Many years before Numbers 16, Moses himself had said, "Yahweh your God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from your midst, from your brethren. Him you shall hear" (Deuteronomy 18:15). And Yahweh confirmed it, "I will raise up for them a Prophet like you from among their brethren, and will put My words in His mouth, and He shall speak to them all that I command Him" (Deuteronomy 18:18). The New Testament tells us plainly who that Prophet is. Peter declared, "Moses truly said to the fathers, 'Yahweh your God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from your brethren. Him you shall hear in all things'" (Acts 3:22), and Stephen quoted the very same prophecy (Acts 7:37). So when Moses said "a Prophet like me," he was pointing forward to Christ, and Numbers 16 shows us one of the deepest ways in which Christ is like Moses. Moses stood between a guilty people and the judgment they deserved; Christ stands between the New Creation and the holy presence of the Father, for "there is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 2:5).

But here is the great comfort, for Christ is not only like Moses; He is far greater than Moses. Moses was a faithful servant in Yahweh's house, but Christ is the Son over His own house (Hebrews 3:5-6). Moses could pray for Israel, but Moses could not give his own blood to take away their sins; Christ could and did. Moses could send Aaron with a censer into the congregation, but Christ Himself entered the true and heavenly sanctuary. Moses interceded only in moments of crisis, and then his prayer was finished; but of Christ the Scripture says, "He is also able to save to the uttermost those who come to God through Him, since He always lives to make intercession for them" (Hebrews 7:25). Aaron ran into the camp once and stopped one plague; Christ never stops.
His intercession never ceases. Day and night, at the right hand of the Father, our great High Priest is pleading for His people. And so, when we fall, our answer is not to run farther into rebellion, but to run to Him, for John says, "If anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous" (1 John 2:1). What hope this is for every weak and struggling heart. We do not stand before the judgment of God alone. We have Someone greater than Moses standing between us and the wrath we deserve, and He always lives to plead for us.

Yet we must hold this comfort with holy care, for the fact that Christ intercedes for us can never become a license to continue in sin. Aaron's incense stopped the plague, but it was never meant to make the rebellion safe, so that the people could keep on rebelling. The intercession was a mercy calling them back, not a permission to go on as before. And so it is with us. John himself, in the very same breath as he tells us we have an Advocate, first says, "These things I write to you, so that you may not sin" (1 John 2:1). Christ pleads for us so that we may repent and forsake our sin, not so that we may keep it. Paul asks the searching question and answers it plainly, "Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? Certainly not!" (Romans 6:1-2). To say, "I will keep this sin, because Christ is interceding for me anyway," is to trample on the very mercy that would save us. The right response to such an Advocate is not carelessness, but repentance. Because He stands between us and judgment, we turn from our sin, forsake the ways that grieve Him, and come running to Him with a heart ready to obey. So let us hear this Prophet like Moses, follow His humility, learn to intercede even for those who oppose us, and rest in the hope that our great High Priest ever lives to plead for us, while we turn away, day by day, from everything He died to cleanse.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, who promised to raise up a Prophet like Moses and kept Your word in Christ,

We thank You that we do not stand before Your judgment alone.

Moses fell on his face for a rebellious people, but Christ always lives to intercede for us.

What hope this gives us, that One greater than Moses stands between us and the wrath we deserve.

Keep us from ever turning this mercy into a license to continue in sin.

Because He pleads for us, make us quick to repent and to forsake the ways that grieve Him.

"He is able to save to the uttermost those who come to God through Him, since He always lives to make intercession for them." - Hebrews 7:25

In Christ’s name we pray. Amen.
